newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ALEX RODRIGUEZ IS THIRD-YOUNGEST BATTING TITLE WINNER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALEX RODRIGUEZ IS THIRD-YOUNGEST BATTING TITLE WINNER.

text.p: The Seattle Mariners' 21-year-old shortstop Alex Rodriguez won the American League batting title with a .358 average Sunday, becoming the third youngest player and first shortstop in 52 years to take the prize.
Al Kaline of the Detroit Tigers was the youngest A.L. batting champ, winning it when he was 20 in 1955. Ty Cobb, another 20-year-old, was the second youngest in 1907.
Cleveland's Lou Boudreaux in 1944 was the last shortstop to win the batting title.
Heading the home run list in a longball year was the Athletics' Mark McGwire, who took advantage of the now enclosed Oakland Coliseum to launch a major league high 52 homers despite missing 31 games.
McGwire, who won the 1987 homer title with 49 in his rookie year, batted just 423 times, giving him a home run clip of one every 8.13 at-bats -- better than Babe Ruth.
Joining McGwire in the 50-homer club was the Baltimore Orioles' Brady Anderson, whose 12th leadoff homer Sunday against Toronto was his 50th overall.
Ken Griffey Jr, Rodriguez's Seattle teammate, needed one more homer to reach 50 and batted leadoff against Oakland Sunday to get more chances, but went hitless in four at-bats.

Cleveland's Albert Belle drove in 148 runs, four more than Juan Gonzalez of Texas and the most in the American League since a pair of Boston Red Sox, Ted Williams and Vern Stephens, knocked in 159 apiece in 1949.
Belle tied with Boston's Mo Vaughn for last season's RBI title and won the crown in 1993.
Belle's teammate Kenny Lofton claimed his fifth straight stolen base title by swiping a career-high 75 bases.
On the pitching side, Andy Pettitte of the New York Yankees looks likely to win his first Cy Young Award but statistically will head only the wins list with 21.

Juan Guzman of the Toronto Blue Jays, who has not pitched since the first day of September, has the ERA title locked up with a 2.93 mark. He is the only American League starter with a mark under 3.00. His teammate Pat Hentgen won his 20th game Sunday and finished with a 3.22 ERA. Pettitte finished at 3.87.
Another Yankee, John Wetteland, has 43 saves for his first such crown.
Roger Clemens of the Boston Red Sox made his struggle to a 10-13 record pay off with his third strikeout title. Clemens, who claimed the crown in 1988 and 1991, registered 257 strikeouts.
